passage: Unlike most songbirds, which learn their songs during a brief window early in life, canaries can add new syllables to their repertoires each breeding season. Neuroscientist Fernando Nottebohm found that, in canaries, a brain region involved in song production grows in spring and shrinks in late summer, and that new neurons are added to it each year. The discovery helped overturn the long-held belief that adult vertebrate brains cannot produce new neurons.
stem: Which choice best describes the significance of Nottebohm's discovery, as presented in the text?
choices: It provided evidence against the idea that adult vertebrates cannot grow new neurons.
It showed that canaries learn their songs during a brief window early in life.
It revealed that most songbirds add new syllables to their songs every year.
It demonstrated that brain regions in songbirds stay the same size all year.
steps: The last sentence states the significance: the discovery helped overturn the belief that adult vertebrate brains can't make new neurons.
The other choices reverse details: canaries are the exception to early-only learning, most songbirds do not keep adding syllables, and the region changes size.
key: “Significance” questions point to the sentence that says why a finding matters.
